To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the agents are able to find trustworthy service providers in a distributed system of agents that are autonomous, have no central trusted authority and have limited knowledge about the trustworthiness and the services offered by other agents.
the agents are able to find trustworthy service providers in a distributed system where there is no central authority and where there are no direct links between all pairs of agents.

the agents can help each other determine trustworthiness of service providers, that the process of trust determination is iterative and that it is possible to aggregate the results of these iterations to obtain a single measure of trust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a distributed system of agents, each of which has its own set of users, who wish to find services provided by agents other than themselves.
the problem of determining trustworthiness of agents and the problem of aggregating information about trustworthiness in a distributed agent environment.
the following issues: how do we model trust, how do agents reason about trust, how do they communicate trust information and how do they use it to make trust decisions?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a novel and interesting method for determining trustworthiness of agents in an environment where there is no centralised trusted authority and agents are autonomous.
this is an important area, and that the paper is a very good start on the road towards a comprehensive solution.

there is not enough evidence to suggest that the use of a distributed agent system for the representation and aggregation of trust in the context of service discovery would have a significant effect on the performance of the system in terms of its ability to provide a trustworthy service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an agent based trust model that is capable of representing and aggregating the trust values in a distributed system.
we have designed, implemented and evaluated the use of a novel trust model and aggregation technique for a distributed multi-agent system.
the agents need to be able to aggregate the trustworthiness information from the various referrals in order to identify trustworthy service providers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distributed trust management system can be implemented without requiring a global trusted authority.
a system of autonomous, self-interested agents can achieve a level of trustworthiness comparable to that achieved by a centralized authority.
a system of agents can be used to aggregate trust information in a way that is more efficient, accurate and robust than a system that relies on the users of the system to aggregate trust information.
